reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Omega be a measurable space and S a compact second-countable topological space equipped with its Borel measurable structure. Let P be a probability measure on Omega and X:NNReal x Omega->S be jointly measurable. Let g:S->R be continuous, and A:NNReal x S->R jointly measurable. Assume that for every T>=0 there exists a real C_T with |A(t,w)|<=C_T for all nonnegative t<=T and all w in S. Suppose that for every t>=0 there exists an integrable real random variable Z_t of mean zero such that, for P-almost every omega, g(X(t,omega))-g(X(0,omega)) = Integral_0^t A(v.toNNReal,X(v.toNNReal,omega)) dv + Z_t(omega). Define the true marginal law rho(t)=(X(t,.))_*P for t in NNReal. For real r, put r_+=r.toNNReal=max(r,0), F(r)=Integral_S g(w) d rho(r_+)(w), and B(r)=Integral_S A(r_+,w) d rho(r_+)(w). Then B is locally Lebesgue integrable on all R; for every a,b in NNReal, F(b)-F(a)=Integral_a^b B(v) dv with the oriented interval integral; for every T in NNReal, F is absolutely continuous on [0,T]; and for Lebesgue-almost every real t>0, F has the full two-sided real derivative F'(t)=B(t). Here absolute continuity has the supplied finite-disjoint-interval meaning: for every epsilon>0 there exists delta>0 such that, for every finite family of endpoint pairs (u_i,v_i) in [0,T] whose unordered half-open intervals (min(u_i,v_i),max(u_i,v_i)] are pairwise disjoint, sum_i |u_i-v_i|<delta implies sum_i |F(u_i)-F(v_i)|<epsilon.
objects: Measurable sample space Omega; compact second-countable Borel state space S; probability measure P.
Jointly measurable process X; continuous test function g; jointly measurable drift A with a uniform state bound on each finite time interval.
For each nonnegative time t, an existential integrable centered variable Z_t.
True marginal laws rho(t)=P.map(X(t,.)); real functions F and B obtained by clamping their time argument to NNReal.
domains: Original time is NNReal; real integration variables and the domains of F,B are all R.
For real r, toNNReal clamps negative r to zero. Thus F(r)=F(0) and B(r)=B(0) when r<0.
The final derivative equality is for volume.restrict(Ioi 0), hence only AE strictly positive real time.
Absolute-continuity endpoint pairs lie in uIcc 0 T=[0,T].
quantifiers: Uniform bound: forall T in NNReal, exists C_T in R, forall t<=T, forall w in S, |A(t,w)|<=C_T.
Balance: forall t in NNReal, exists Z_t, Integrable Z_t and mean(Z_t)=0 and AE omega the indicated identity holds.
The exceptional sample set in the balance may depend on t; no single full-measure set valid at every t is given.
Conclusions: B is locally integrable; forall nonnegative a,b the balance holds; forall T>=0 absolute continuity holds; AE t>0 HasDerivAt F (B t) t.
Absolute continuity: forall epsilon>0, exists delta>0, forall finite admissible pair families, small summed lengths imply small summed F-increments.
assumptions: S is compact and second-countable with BorelSpace; no PseudoMetrizableSpace assumption is explicit.
P is a probability measure; X and A are jointly measurable on their stated product domains.
A is uniformly bounded over all states on each nonnegative finite horizon.
At each nonnegative time the increment from zero is the oriented drift integral plus some integrable zero-mean variable, AE in omega.
No filtration, martingale, independent increments, path continuity, or continuity of A in time is assumed.
conclusion: B belongs to LocallyIntegrable(volume) on the entire real line.
For every a,b in NNReal, F(b)-F(a)=Integral_a^b B.
For every T in NNReal, AbsolutelyContinuousOnInterval F 0 T, with the exact finite-family condition decoded in the theorem text.
For Lebesgue-AE t>0, HasDerivAt F (B t) t.
scopes: The approved hSlice is precisely measurability of omega->X(t,omega) obtained by composing joint measurability with omega->(t,omega).
The approved rho definition is precisely pushforward P by X t; no map body remains suppressed.
The two real functions use the same clamped marginal rho(r.toNNReal); B additionally uses A at that same clamped time.
Negative times are included in local integrability but excluded from the AE derivative-equals-B conclusion.
The absolute-continuity predicate sums ordinary distances, which are absolute values for real F; it does not require pair endpoints to be listed in increasing order.
constant_dependencies: The horizon bound C_T may depend on T and A (and the given state space); it is common to every t<=T and every w. No global-in-T constant is asserted.
The variables Z_t may depend on t and all the data; no joint measurability of (t,omega)->Z_t(omega) or common witness is claimed.
The delta in absolute continuity can depend on epsilon,T,F; it is uniform over all admissible finite interval families.
No quantitative derivative, error, or norm bound is part of the conclusion.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: Every displayed integral formally uses Lean's totalized real Bochner integral. Here compactness and continuity make g bounded and integrable under every rho(t); measurability and the bound with horizon T=t make A(t,.) bounded and integrable under every rho(t). The final B is locally integrable, so its finite oriented integrals are genuine. Joint measurability and the uniform horizon bound likewise make every sample-path finite-horizon drift integral integrable. There is no missing integrability premise for the law expectations.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: Input order is forall t exists Z_t AE omega; this gives neither a jointly measurable Z process nor an event of probability one on which all time identities hold simultaneously. The law balance is pointwise for every pair a,b. The derivative equality is AE strictly positive real t.
semantic_checks.pushforwards: Verified explicitly from approved hSlice and rho expansions: rho(t)=(X t)_*P. Both F and B use rho of the clamped time.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: Balance conclusion permits any a,b in NNReal, including a>b, with sign reversal for the oriented integral. Absolute-continuity admissibility uses uIcc endpoints and pairwise-disjoint uIoc subintervals, so lengths are absolute and interval-pair orientation is immaterial.
semantic_checks.exponents: No p-exponent, squares or higher moments. The absolute-continuity sums use distances to power one.
semantic_checks.compactness: CompactSpace and SecondCountableTopology on S are explicit; no metric or pseudometric structure on S is required by the statement. F is real-valued, so its absolute-continuity predicate uses the ordinary real metric.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: T=0, t=0, a=0, b=0, and a=b are all admitted. F and B have constant extensions to negative time. No derivative identity at t=0 is asserted. B(0) need not be zero, so the constant negative-time F cannot be claimed to have derivative B there.
semantic_checks.absolute_continuity: The refreshed approved context fully specifies totalLengthFilter as the comap of neighborhoods of zero under sum of endpoint distances, and disjWithin as endpoints in uIcc with pairwise-disjoint uIoc intervals. This verifies the usual epsilon-delta finite-interval absolute-continuity meaning on [0,T], including endpoint behavior.
semantic_checks.derivative_domain: HasDerivAt is the full two-sided derivative of the real-domain F. The qualifier is AE t in (0,infinity), not a derivative within NNReal, not pointwise at every positive t, and not a claim at or below zero.
